title: The corridor (Avot 4:16)
hook: the backstage hallway before the curtain: this world is like a corridor before the banquet hall; prepare in the corridor
tomorrow: if this is just the hallway, does any hour here count?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Matya ben Charash: be first to greet every person, and be a tail to lions. Greet first. Now, a hallway.

The hallway before the curtain smells like hairspray and dust and somebody's orange. The lights are low. Through the wall, the murmur of a full house, a cough, a program dropped. Everyone back here is doing something small: checking a prop, fixing a collar, mouthing a first line. What do you do in the hallway before the curtain? A sage in Avot says that's the question of a whole life.
screen: `HAIRSPRAY, DUST, AN ORANGE.` → `THE MURMUR THROUGH THE WALL.` → `WHAT DO YOU DO IN THE HALLWAY?`

segments.voice: Rabbi Yaakov says it in two lines. This world is like a corridor before the world to come. Prepare yourself in the corridor, so that you may enter the banquet hall. The Hebrew words are a picture. The corridor is the prozdor, the entrance passage. The banquet hall is the traklin, the great dining room, where the feast is laid. In Rabbi Yaakov's picture, you don't live in the hallway forever, and you don't skip it either. You get ready in it. So what does getting ready look like? Here's what's surprising: it's small. A collar straightened. A line said once more. A prop put where your hand will find it in the dark. Nobody in the audience will ever see the corridor, and every good moment on stage was made there. Jewish teaching holds a range of views about what the world to come is like, and this saying doesn't describe it. It describes the hallway, and what to do in it. One caution: some people hear corridor and think this world doesn't matter, it's just a passage. Avot's very next saying will push hard on that reading. For today, the job is simple. Prepare in the corridor.
screen: `THIS WORLD: A CORRIDOR.` · `PROZDOR AND TRAKLIN.` · `GETTING READY IS SMALL.` · `THE SAYING DESCRIBES THE HALLWAY.` · then, large: `PREPARE IN THE CORRIDOR.`

segments.voice: Get one small thing ready for tomorrow, right now: your keys by the door, a glass of water by the bed, the shoes you'll wear. Hold it a moment, feel its weight and texture, and set it exactly where your hand will find it. Then sit back down for the rest of the sit, in your own corridor.
screen: `ONE THING FOR TOMORROW.` · `FEEL ITS WEIGHT.` · `SET IT WHERE YOUR HAND WILL FIND IT.`

segments.voice: The corridor. Rabbi Yaakov: this world is like a corridor before the world to come; prepare yourself there, for the banquet hall.
Pocket this: prepare in the corridor, where nobody sees and everything is made. Forty of sixty: places, please.

howItsDone: Many Jews prepare for Shabbat in the hours before it begins, cooking, cleaning and setting the table, and the tradition often reads that weekly getting-ready as a picture of preparing in this world.
